question.stem: An electric scooter starts from rest. The graph shows how its velocity changes with time during the first 12 s.
question.diagramAlt: Velocity in metres per second against time in seconds from 0 to 12, on a grid of 1 second by 1 metre per second squares. The curve starts at the origin, rises steeply, and bends over so that it levels off towards 12 metres per second. At 8 seconds the velocity is about 10.4 metres per second.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Describe how the acceleration of the scooter changes during the first 12 s.
markscheme: because the gradient of the graph decreases, approaching zero as the velocity approaches a constant value ✓

parts.label: b
parts.question: Estimate the distance travelled by the scooter in the first 8.0 s.
markscheme: the distance is the area under the graph from 0 to 8.0 s ✓
area estimated by counting squares (each square = 1 m) OR by splitting into strips/trapezia ✓
Accept 50.1 to 58.9 m. Award [2 max] for ½ × 10.4 × 8.0 = 41.5 m (curve treated as a straight line).

mistakes.feedback: The graph is a curve, not a straight line: it lies above the straight line from the origin, so the area is larger than ½ × v × t. Count the squares under the curve.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Calculate the average acceleration of the scooter during the first 8.0 s.
markscheme: $a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{10.4}{8.0} = 1.3\ \text{m s}^{-2}$; allow a velocity read from the graph between 10 and 11 $\text{m s}^{-1}$ ✓

parts.label: d
parts.question: Explain why the acceleration of the scooter just after it starts is greater than your answer to (c).
markscheme: the gradient of the curve (the tangent) is steepest at the start ✓
the average acceleration is the gradient of the straight line from the origin to the point at 8.0 s, which is less steep than the tangent at the start ✓

vmax.what: speed the scooter approaches (used to draw the graph)

tau.what: time constant of the curve (used to draw the graph only)

t8.what: time for the distance and average acceleration

parts.label: a
parts.examinerNote: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity–time graph; the curve flattens. "The scooter slows down" earns nothing: the velocity still increases.

parts.label: b
parts.examinerNote: The exact area is from the generating function. Square counting by students usually lands within about 5 %; the accept range is 8 %.

parts.label: c
parts.examinerNote: Average acceleration uses the change in velocity over the whole interval (the chord), not the gradient at one point.

parts.label: d
parts.examinerNote: Instantaneous acceleration = gradient of the tangent; average = gradient of the chord. At t = 0 the tangent gradient is vmax/τ = 3.0 m s⁻² (shown in the audit as a0).
